raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Preserve real LoRA adapters during idle DP forwards and resolve gathered MoE tokens against each receiver's adapter slots. This is the follow-up discussed with @almogtavor in #61453, building on #61714.

**Depends on #61714.** Its commit is retained as a separate prerequisite; the [follow-up-only diff](https://github.com/MagellaX/vllm/commit/faf4a54103bee17f479786226c551404427e93ef) is separate from its active-peer fix. Both commits are rebased onto main at `3fbc8d8b`; I'll drop the prerequisite commit after #61714 lands. This covers already-resident adapters, not a distributed loading/eviction protocol or #59819's slot-weight API.

**Overlap:** #63526 also addresses idle-adapter preservation. This PR additionally remaps gathered logical adapter IDs to receiver-local slots and covers opposite load orders in DP serving. The shared lifecycle changes need sequencing with #63526; they are not claimed as a separate missing fix. I can drop that part here after #63526 lands while retaining the remapping and its regressions.

## Claims

- First and repeated idle forwards no longer create zero-weight warmup adapters or remove real adapters. Profiling, warmup and capture keep their existing lifecycle.
- The naive DP/EP dispatch carries int64 adapter IDs, then remaps them to receiver-local slots on GPU. Different load orders no longer mix expert deltas; missing residency triggers a device-side assertion.
- Regression coverage includes both model runners, pinned/unpinned adapters, opposite slot orders, large IDs, stale padded metadata and CUDA graph replay.

## Validation

GPU results below were recorded on pre-rebase commit `d6c3e33` over #61714's `36ebc0a`, not the original author's test counts. The PR is now rebased onto `3fbc8d8b`; rebase checks and the upstream idle-scheduling adaptation are described below. The GPU matrix has not been rerun on this base. Model: `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct` with `jeeejeee/olmoe-instruct-text2sql-spider`, rank 8, nonzero expert B weights.

| Hardware | Configuration / check | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H100, 2-GPU allocation | 8 single-GPU lifecycle cases; DP2×TP1 serving in both runners | 10 passed; exact before/after lifecycle scores and SQL expectations |
| H100, 2-GPU allocation | CPU/CUDA mapping and metadata cases, actual graph capture/replay; DP2 serving with two distinct adapters and reversed peer slots | 9 unit/graph cases + 1 serving case passed; both adapters' scores unchanged on both DP ranks |
| H100, 4 GPUs | DP2×TP2, default eager vs batch-invariant eager, three trials each on the same four devices | Batch-invariant scores exactly equal across all peer conditions; 4/4 SQL outputs passed in each mode; `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` enabled |
| H200, 4 GPUs | Same paired DP2×TP2 experiment, three trials each on the same four devices | Batch-invariant scores exactly equal across all peer conditions; 4/4 SQL outputs passed in each mode |
| H100, 4 GPUs | Earlier default compiled/graph-enabled DP2×TP2 serving experiment | Peer-state score differences below the measured repeated-reference noise; graph capture completed |

The paired experiments compare 761 teacher-forced token scores on DP rank 0 while rank 1 is first idle, adapter-busy, repeatedly adapter-busy, base-only busy, then idle again. All 16 background streams must be decoding throughout each busy probe. Saved vectors, token IDs, hardware UUIDs and executed-source hashes were independently checked. Deterministic eager had zero mean and maximum differences, including between trials, on **each hardware separately**; this is not a claim that H100 and H200 scores match each other.

Default eager remains numerically variable. Mean absolute score deltas versus the adapter-busy reference (nats, averaged over three trials):

| Peer condition | H100 default eager | H200 default eager | Batch-invariant eager, H100 / H200 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First idle | 0.023476 | 0.059572 | 0 / 0 |
| Adapter-busy repeat noise | 0.021780 | 0.043830 | 0 / 0 |
| Base-only busy | 0.040148 | 0.057005 | 0 / 0 |
| Idle after activity | 0.046066 | 0.011604 | 0 / 0 |

No numerical tolerance or global kernel default was changed. Exact comparisons use the existing `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` mode; the docs explain its trade-offs. SQL outputs matched the existing four expectations in both modes on both GPU types. This is targeted correctness validation, not a throughput benchmark or a full vLLM suite run.

Full repository pre-commit checks passed on the changed files in Linux, including mypy and Buildkite test selection. After adding test-only typing annotations, the nine mapping/graph cases and the failing/passing opposite-slot serving controls were rerun on H100s; production sources remained unchanged.

Rebase checks on `faf4a541` (2026-11-02): all applicable Linux pre-commit hooks passed on all 14 changed files, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering. The validation snapshot's Git tree exactly matches this head. Six direct CPU checks using real Torch/leaf modules passed (slot remapping, missing residency, no-LoRA metadata, and upstream bgmv); this was not a full pytest run. All three changed test files are AST-identical to the previous head. The conflict resolution preserves main's #64457 offline-DP scheduling change instead of restoring its removed model-runner dummy forward. The rest of the runtime patch is unchanged. No GPUs were reserved, and the H100/H200 results above remain historical.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and controls</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v tests/lora/test_worker.py::test_idle_step_preserves_loaded_lora
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v tests/lora/test_olmoe_tp.py::test_olmoe_lora_idle_peer
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py -k dispatched_lora
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v tests/lora/test_olmoe_tp.py::test_olmoe_lora_slot_order
```

The lifecycle test fails on #61714 alone because the first dummy forward evicts adapter 1. Retaining the idle fix but restoring source-slot dispatch makes the opposite-slot serving test fail with changed SQL-adapter scores. Both controls fail at the intended assertions.

Paired server configuration, repeated with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0` and `1` in fresh servers on the same allocation:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct \
  --api-server-count 1 --data-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-lora --max-loras 1 --max-lora-rank 8 \
  --lora-modules sql=/path/to/adapter --max-model-len 1024 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --enforce-eager
```

Use `PROMPTS` from `tests/lora/test_olmoe_tp.py`, `prompt_logprobs=0`, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=1`, and `X-data-parallel-rank: 0` for scores. Background load is 16 greedy streams pinned to rank 1, `ignore_eos=true`, `min_tokens=max_tokens=768`. Repeat each condition three times; compare actual prompt-token identities as well as scores. Also generate the full four SQL outputs with `max_tokens=64`.

Pinned revisions: model `b89a7c4bc24fb9e55ce2543c9458ce0ca5c4650e`; adapter `173c24a401b96703ba97256d5a2f4d4c4c1915a6`. Linux CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Triton 3.8, Transformers 5.19.0. Native extensions came from the matching prerequisite base `7840bede9`; the changes here are Python-only. NVLink, mutual CUDA peer access and exact NCCL all-reduce/all-gather checks passed before the multi-GPU experiments.

The graph unit directly captures and replays changed slot metadata. The graph-enabled serving run completed capture and scoring, but ended before the periodic replay counter was emitted; no measured serving replay count is claimed.

</details>

## Details

Idle runtime forwards used the warmup adapter setup/cleanup path. An explicit idle flag now selects a local no-LoRA mapping without touching resident weights, shared by MRV1 and MRV2. MRV1 still has the same bug in supported deployments, so it needs the fix too.

Gathering sender-local slot indices is unsafe when ranks load the same adapters in different orders. Persistent GPU ID tables and a receiver-local remap preserve identities without adding a per-layer CPU collective or host readback. This adds metadata copies and GPU remapping; no throughput improvement is claimed.

All participating workers must already hold identical weights for each adapter ID, and `max_loras` must fit that resident set. The device assertion is a fail-closed check, not coordinated admission. Dynamic eviction, concurrent hot updates, multi-node deployments, EP serving, Blackwell TRT-LLM, AMD/XPU and a full external-launcher deployment were not validated. The source-selection rules wire the added regressions into the existing LoRA CI steps.

---

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

 ## Using Tips
 
+### Idle data-parallel workers
+
+Idle data-parallel workers still run forwards to participate in MoE collectives.
+These forwards use no adapter for their dummy tokens and preserve loaded adapters;
+they do not perform the dummy-adapter setup and cleanup used during warmup.
+
+Dispatched tokens carry adapter identities, which each receiving worker translates
+into its own GPU slots. Adapters can therefore occupy different slots on different
+workers. The same adapter weights must still be resident on every worker that
+processes its tokens. Loading an adapter on only one rank is insufficient.
+
+Residency, eviction and in-place weight updates are not coordinated by this
+mapping. Preload the participating adapter set on all workers and keep it resident
+while requests run; `max_loras` must accommodate that set on each worker.
+
+Adapter preservation does not guarantee bitwise-identical floating-point results
+across changing peer workloads. For deterministic score comparisons on supported
+configurations, enable `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`; see [batch invariance](batch_invariance.md)
+for its limits and performance trade-offs. `--enforce-eager` alone does not make
+execution batch-invariant.
+
